input.rationale: Article 12.1 contains a two-way indemnity with proper procedure (notice, control of defence, cooperation, settlement consent), so SFJ does indemnify us for its gross negligence/wilful misconduct, material breach, Protocol breach and AZ License breach. However, the third-party IP infringement risk runs only one way: SFJ's indemnity in 12.1.1 contains no IP element, while our indemnity in 12.1.2(f) covers infringement "by either Party in performing its duties or obligations hereunder" — i.e. we indemnify SFJ even for infringement caused by SFJ's own performance, subject only to a gross negligence/wilful misconduct/material breach carve-out. Article 11.3.2 confirms there is no counterparty IP indemnity elsewhere. That fails the fallback (counterparty IP indemnity absent; customer indemnity not narrow) under the detection guidance. The minimal fix keeps our indemnity for the Product and our own performance (appropriate since PB owns and supplies the Product) and adds a mirror SFJ IP indemnity for SFJ's own activities.

proposal.summary: Add SFJ IP-infringement indemnity for SFJ's own activities and narrow PB's IP indemnity so it no longer covers SFJ's performance
proposal.comment: [Playbook] Our position is that each party's IP indemnity should track its own activities: we have added an SFJ indemnity for third-party IP claims arising from SFJ's (and its Affiliates'/Permitted Third Parties') performance, and narrowed Section 12.1.2(f) so PB no longer indemnifies SFJ for infringement caused by SFJ's own conduct. We remain comfortable indemnifying for the Product itself and for PB's own performance.
